references.text: Listen of the heads of the fathers' houses in Israel, showing the leaders of the tribes and their genealogies.
The twelve tribal princes who were to assist Moses with the census, one from each tribe.
The organization of the twelve tribes in the camp, each under its own banner and leader.
The princes of Israel, heads of the fathers' houses, who were tribal leaders and stood over those who were numbered.
Continuation of the account where Moses gathered twelve staffs, one for each tribe, and Aaron's staff sprouted.
The twelve tribes of Israel, which form the basis for the division of the tribes with their princes.
The twelve stones on the breastplate engraved with the names of the twelve tribes of Israel.
Aaron's staff that sprouted is mentioned as one of the items in the ark of the covenant.
